symbol_location2 = us | symbol3 = yes | symbol_location3 = ace }} The '''Santa Clara Transit Center''' (also called '''Santa Clara–University''' by Capitol Corridor) is a railway station in downtown [[Santa Clara, California]]. It is served by [[Caltrain]], [[Amtrak]] ''[[Capitol Corridor]]'', and [[Altamont Corridor Express]] (ACE) trains. It is the planned terminus for the [[Silicon Valley BART extension]] into Santa Clara County on the future Green and Orange Lines. The former station building, constructed in 1863 by the [[San Francisco and San Jose Railroad]], is used by the '''South Bay Historical Railroad Society''' as the '''Edward Peterman Museum of Railroad History'''. == Station design == [[File:Caltrain and ACE at Santa Clara.jpg|thumb|left|Caltrain (left) and ACE trains at the station]] The station is an [[transport hub|intermodal transportation center]], with [[Caltrain]] and [[Altamont Corridor Express]] train service and bus service operated by the [[Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority]] (VTA). The station is served by [[Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority|VTA Bus]] routes {{VTA bus route|21}}, {{VTA bus route|22}}, {{VTA bus route|53}}, {{VTA bus route|59}}, {{VTA bus route|60}} to [[San José International Airport#Ground transportation|San José International Airport]], and Rapid {{VTA bus route|522}}. The station has a side platform serving the southbound Caltrain track (Track 3) and an island platform for the northbound Caltrain track (Track 2) and the ACE/Amtrak track (Track 1), allowing [[Cross-platform interchange|cross-platform transfer]]. The island platform is connected to the side platform by a pedestrian tunnel that was completed in 2012. Additional tracks northeast of Track 1 are used by [[Union Pacific]] freight trains. {{clear left}} == History == [[File:Coast Daylight at Santa Clara station, April 1971.jpg|thumb|left|The ''Coast Daylight'' at Santa Clara in 1971]] [[File:Santa Clara station, May 25, 1974.jpg|thumb|left|The station building in 1974]] The Santa Clara depot, built by the [[San Francisco and San Jose Railroad]] in late 1863, was the oldest continuously operating railroad depot in the State of California until the ticket office was closed in May 1997. The original {{convert|24x50|ft|adj=mid}} board and [[batten]] depot was one of the two "way stations" built between [[San Francisco]] and [[San Jose, California|San Jose]]. Plans for a railroad linking San Francisco and San Jose began as early as 1851. Though the 1851 scheme ultimately failed, the incorporation of the San Francisco and San Jose Railroad in 1859 met with success. Most of the financing for the project came from county government in San Francisco, [[San Mateo County, California|San Mateo]] and [[Santa Clara County, California|Santa Clara]] counties, with the [[University of Santa Clara]] and local industry also playing a significant role in both [[Share capital|stock]] acquisition and choice of placement of the depot in Santa Clara. The first passenger service to San Francisco started on December 28, 1893,{{cite news |title=The Cars Reach Santa Clara |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-san-francisco-call-bulletin-the-cars/197891935/ |access-date=20 May 2026 |newspaper=Daily Morning Call |date=December 27, 1863 |location=San Francisco, California |page=1 |via=Newspapers.com}} with the final few miles to San Jose completed the following month. The [[Southern Pacific Railroad]] acquired the San Francisco & San Jose Railroad in 1868. The depot, originally on the east side of the tracks, was moved to its present location in 1877 and attached to the existing {{convert|32x50|ft|adj=mid}} freight house constructed several years earlier. Because of the large volume of agricultural freight shipped from the depot, the freight house was increased in size at that time to its present dimensions of {{convert|32x160|ft}}. On November 1, 1877, the ''[[San Jose Mercury]]'' reported the facility nearing completion. Following construction of the railroad, farming and fruit-related industries developed in the Santa Clara area, with the depot serving as a focal point for shipping. Rail service provided the direct link to San Francisco and, in the later 1870s, to [[Southern California]]. Typical of these efforts were those of [[James A. Dawson]], who pioneered the area's fruit-canning industry in 1871. By the turn of the century, the Pratt-Low Preserving Company, the largest fruit packing plant in central California, was located just south of the depot. [[Caltrans]] acquired the depot from Southern Pacific in 1980. It was placed in the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 1985. In cooperation with the [[South Bay Historical Railroad Society]], a nonprofit group founded the same year, they began renovation work in 1986 on the depot, by then badly in need of repair. A group of volunteers spent over 25,000 hours hauling away debris, replacing support timbers, [[siding (construction)|siding]], exterior decking and interior flooring, scraping peeling paint, painting and many other repairs. With the major renovation complete since 1992, this 156-year-old building hosts a railroad library and museum with 2 large model railroad layouts and many other artifacts while still serving its original function as a passenger depot. Santa Clara was added as a station for the [[Altamont Corridor Express]] (ACE) on March 5, 2001. ACE service to the station was discontinued on July 29, 2005, to allow for platform construction. ACE service to Santa Clara resumed on May 14, 2012; Amtrak ''Capitol Corridor'' trains began stopping at the station on May 21.{{Vurek-Capitol Corridor}}{{rp|9}}{{cite web |url=https://www.greatamericanstations.com/stations/santa-clara-university-ca-scc/ |title=Santa Clara, CA – Transit Center (SCC) |publisher=Amtrak |work=Great American Stations}}{{cite web |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508074128/http://www.acerail.com/Home.aspx |archive-date=May 8, 2012 |url=http://www.acerail.com/Home.aspx |title=ACE {{!}} Altamont Corridor Express |publisher=San Joaquin Regional Rail Commission}} {{As of|2024}}, Amtrak plans to modify the platform for [[accessibility]] by FY 2025.{{cite web |url=https://www.amtrak.com/content/dam/projects/dotcom/english/public/documents/corporate/statefactsheets/CALIFORNIA23.pdf |title=Amtrak Fact Sheet Fiscal Year 2023 State of California |page=8 |publisher=Amtrak |date=March 2024}} === Future === Santa Clara is planned to be the [[terminal station]] for the second phase of the [[Silicon Valley BART extension]]. Santa Clara was chosen as the terminal because of the access to the San Jose International Airport as well as the proposed BART maintenance facility located in the vicinity of the station at the former [[Union Pacific]] rail yard. A new island platform will be constructed with a pedestrian underpass. An 800-space parking facility is included in the plans, and VTA is expected to [[transit oriented development|develop transit oriented spaces]] adjacent the station.{{cite web |title=Santa Clara Station |url=https://vtaorgcontent.s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/Site_Content/BART_Phase2_Stations_SantaClara.pdf |publisher=VTA |access-date=29 May 2019}}[http://www.vta.org/bart/documents/other/bart_fact.pdf BART Silicon Valley Fact Sheet]. BART.gov. 2011. {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100711130539/http://www.vta.org/bart/documents/other/bart_fact.pdf |date= July 11, 2010 }} The station was considered for [[California High-Speed Rail]], but was rejected on the grounds that it was too close to the nearby, and much larger, [[Diridon Station]] in [[San Jose, California|San Jose]], and that the airport traffic that it would receive would not be enough to justify maintaining a separate station. It was also considered as the terminal for a [[people mover]] to the airport; however, San Jose Diridon was later chosen as the terminal.{{cite news |url=https://sanjosespotlight.com/san-jose-opens-door-to-norm-mineta-international-airport-connector-proposals-development-rfp-accepting-bids-people-mover-public-transportation-transit/ |title=San Jose opens door to airport connector proposals |first=Eli |last=Wolfe |date=May 18, 2022 |newspaper=San Jose Spotlight |access-date=June 24, 2022}} == References == {{NPS}} {{reflist}} == External links == {{Commons category}} *[https://acerail.com/stations/ Santa Clara – ACE] {{Amtrak web|SCC|Santa Clara, CA–Transit Center}} *[https://www.caltrain.com/stations/santaclarastation.html Santa Clara – Caltrain] *[https://www.vta.org/go/stations/santa-clara-transit-center Santa Clara Transit Center – VTA] *[https://www.sbhrs.org/ South Bay Historical Railroad Society] {{navboxes|list= {{Bay Area Rapid Transit}} {{Caltrain}} {{Altamont Corridor Express navbox}} {{Amtrak California stations}} {{Bay Area Rail Stations}} {{SP Coast Line stations}} {{National Register of Historic Places in California}} {{Santa Clara University}} }} {{authority control}} [[Category:Amtrak stations in Santa Clara County, California]] [[Category:Caltrain stations in Santa Clara County, California]] [[Category:Altamont Corridor Express stations in Santa Clara County, California]] [[Category:Former Southern Pacific Railroad stations in California]] [[Category:National Register of Historic Places in Santa Clara County, California]] [[Category:Railway stations in the United States opened in 1864]] [[Category:Railway stations on the National Register of Historic Places in California]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Santa Clara, California]] [[Category:Railroad museums in California]] [[Category:Railway stations in California at university and college campuses]] [[Category:Future Bay Area Rapid Transit stations]]
